steps: 1 Resolve sources: for every source of the group fetch the OCR text (fetch_text.py), pin it in data2/sources/<id>.json with the rights facts of the item metadata, write the volume-to-unit map (printed pages or leaf ranges per unit) into the ledger; a failed lookup is recorded as failed, a blocked host as blocked.

2 Parse: write one parser per layout (flow: lines of the search text; cols: word boxes of the item djvu.xml aligned to the search text, the xml deleted after the run; index: surname entries filtered by unit). A row is exactly what the source prints: name tokens, rank tokens, company from the nearest heading, every other printed token in the remarks, the printed page, the character offset. Never correct, complete, reorder or merge anything.

3 Write: r2lib.write_unit per unit into data2/<army>/<state>/<unit>.jsonl.gz, one segment per source text; a unit with several sources has several segments (a participants list or casualty list is a segment of its own).
4 Verify: verify_unit.py on every file (V1 name, V2 remarks, V3 page, V4 rank); zero V1 or V3 defects; every defect is fixed in the parser, never in the row.

5 Reconcile with the earlier data (rosters/data CSVs): row counts per unit and company, rows only in one of the two readings; write the differences to GOVERNANCE/horde/ws-rosters/<group>/differences.csv; resolve none by guessing.

6 Report: rosters/reports/<group>.md in the section order of reports/union-vt.md (summary, lines per unit against the strength, the unit files and flag codes, sources and rights, checks, anomalies, gaps; numbers computed by a script, never typed), the pointer file rosters/sources/<group>.json (form roster2-sources-pointer/1), tmp/library/rosters/MANIFEST-<group>.json, gaps as lines in rosters/GAPS.md and proposed register entries under GOVERNANCE/horde/ws-rosters/proposed-register/, one dated line in GOVERNANCE/progress.md (printf >>).

7 Close: python3 -I pipeline2/build_index.py --lint (no defect), then GOVERNANCE/horde/ws-rosters/<group>/CLOSED.json as the last file written (form in pipeline2/open_groups.py); the item is then no longer returned by the planning step.
rules: name as printed: the OCR tokens of the source text, joined by single blanks; a garbled name stays garbled and is flagged by the verifier statistics, never repaired
no label of presence: a man is stated present at Gettysburg only where a printed remark, a participants list, a casualty list or a burial list says so; the row carries that statement as printed

rights per name come from the segment: source id, volume and the ledger entry (Internet Archive flag, date, state publication); a modern compilation (Henderson, Manarin, Howard, Broadfoot, Busey and Martin) and a lending-restricted item are never opened

host rules: archive.org only for the OCR text (metadata and /cors/ downloads, one request at a time, 1.2 s apart); a refused or challenged host is recorded as blocked and not retried; no login, no key, no bot-block workaround
disk: OCR text only under tmp/library/rosters; the djvu.xml of a cols source is a transient file deleted after the run; at most about 1 GB per group; delete scratch you no longer need
machine: the 4 shared vCPUs; any job above about 30 s of CPU runs through tools/horde/bench.sh; one cols volume (30 to 80 MB of xml) at a time

unit assignment: a row is filed to a unit only where the source states the unit; an entry that names no Gettysburg unit goes to a list file beside the unit files (data2/<army>/<state>/_other-<source>.jsonl.gz), never to a guessed unit

sidecars (the contract build_index.py --lint checks): <unit>.flags.json.gz, form roster2-flags/1, keys f, u (the unit key), n (the rows of the unit file), codes (the legend of THAT file), ocr_uncertain (row numbers), on_rolls_july_1863 (yes and no, inferred from printed dates only, with its basis and rule), optional unit_file_raw_lines_sha256; <unit>.cells.json.gz, form roster2-cells/1, key rows; derived marks live there and never in a row (DD-ROS-01)

copy audit: printed names such as Claude stay as printed (DD-STG-02 lets the packer pass a name field and a flag file name list); the same word in a remark, a rank, a header, a report in the app or a pointer file is a hit: say in the report which rows hold such printed words

second reading of page images: only through pipeline2/page_image.py (text PDF from archive.org/cors, one request at a time, 1.2 s apart; images transient, never stored; the page routes archive.org/download/<id>/page/ and iiif.archive.org are refused by the proxy)

tasks: A reader for roster2/2 (gunzip with DecompressionStream, one file per unit, no server) and the sidecars named by the index: flags (roster2-flags/1; show the legend of the file, not a fixed table), cells (roster2-cells/1), lists (<unit>.lists.jsonl.gz); tests in app/tests/roster*.test.mjs on the real files.

The page of PLAN.md section 4.2 without per-man presence labels: search by name and unit; the unit page with its segments, sources and rights; the printed remark as printed; a mark where a source states presence (a remark naming Gettysburg, a participants, casualty or burial list); "damaged in the text layer" on ocr_uncertain rows; "on the rolls in July 1863 (inferred from printed dates)" only with its basis; cross-reference lines shown as such; "n present, names not recovered" and the gap id on every unit with a gap.

Rights per name: each row shows its segment source, volume, printed page and the ledger rights text; no file of the page may mention how the data was made (the copy audit allows the printed word in the name field only, DD-STG-02).
gates: keyboard use, phone width, no colour-only marks
no per-man presence label is shown unless a source states it
